headline: The RBI announces its rate decision at 10:00 am today, and most economists expect its first rate rise since 2023. The dashboard is **neutral (+6)**: the price trend is still down, but options traders turned more hopeful after Nifty's 1% bounce to 22,776.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.body:
The data shows Nifty closed at **22,776** yesterday, up 1% for a second day of gains. Even after the bounce, Nifty is still below its 20-day average (23,147), its 50-day average (23,824) and its 200-day average (24,318), and recent peaks and dips are each lower than the ones before. Price-trend score: −2, the lowest possible.
The other checks disagree. In futures, the price rose while open contracts fell 1.2%, a sign that people who bet on a fall were closing those bets. But foreign funds (FIIs) are still mostly betting on a fall, so this check scores 0. In options, sellers added many new puts at 22,300–22,600. They earn money only if Nifty stays above those levels, so this reads as a floor being built (+1.5). The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) jumped from 0.71 to 1.06 in five sessions, which the dashboard reads as bullish (+1).
Added up, the bias score is **+6 out of ±100: neutral**, with the checks pulling in opposite directions, so confidence is low. My read: a relief bounce inside a downtrend, not yet a turn, because no level that defines the downtrend has broken.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.body:
The data shows FIIs **sold ₹2,961 crore** of shares yesterday, while domestic funds (DIIs, such as Indian mutual funds) **bought ₹5,089 crore**, which more than covered the selling. The FII sale is just under the dashboard's ₹3,000 crore 'big day' mark, and the dashboard has only one day of saved cash data, so it can't measure a streak yet.
The longer record shows a trend. NSDL data shows FIIs sold most sectors in the second half of September: financial services −₹6,943 crore, oil and gas −₹4,469 crore, autos −₹3,542 crore, telecom −₹2,423 crore and metals −₹2,322 crore. Since March, they have sold about ₹1.18 lakh crore of financial stocks.
In index futures, FIIs hold only **8.5% of their positions as bets on a rise**, up from 8.0% last week. Two years ago it was near 80%. Below 10% is the zone where FIIs have usually started closing their bets on a fall, which pushes prices up. That hasn't happened yet; a clear rise in this number would be the first sign.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.body:
The dashboard rates the global backdrop as **Headwinds** (4 of 10 signals hurt India, 1 helps). The biggest problem is US interest rates. The US 10-year bond pays **5.27%**, higher than on almost any day in the past year and up about 0.5 points in a month. That gives foreign money less reason to buy Indian shares. The dollar is up 2.7% in a month, and the rupee is weak at **₹96.29 per dollar**., which shrinks foreign investors' returns.
Oil is the second worry: Brent is **$100.8 a barrel**, up 29% in three months, and India imports most of its oil. Some relief: it is down 4% this week, as Middle East exports recover and Europe discusses releasing emergency fuel stocks.
The Fed has raised rates to 3.75–4.00% over six months. Dashboard flags: 6-month US bills pay 4.30%, so markets still expect another US rise, but that expectation eased this week. News reports agree: a weak jobs report cut the odds of an October hike to about 20%. US stocks rose about 0.7–0.9% to **a record high** on Tuesday, helped by lower oil and bond rates. That hasn't stopped FII selling in India.

sections.title: Company results
sections.body: No Nifty 50 company reported in the last 7 days. The dashboard's filings are small companies, many with late June-quarter results; no pattern stands out. The real results season starts with **TCS on Thursday, October 8**. Early business updates look good: HDFC Bank's loans grew 16.3% and its deposits 18.8%, which helped bank shares on Monday.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.body:
**Today, 10:00 am: the RBI decision.** The repo rate is 5.25%. In a Business Standard poll, 8 of 10 economists expect a rise to 5.50%, and a Reuters poll put it near 60%. Inflation was 4.82% in August, above the RBI's 4% target. A rise is mostly expected, so the RBI's hints about more rises may matter more. A tougher message could hit banks and rate-sensitive shares; a pause would surprise.
Later: US Fed meeting minutes (11:30 pm tonight), TCS results (Oct 8), India inflation data and HCL Tech results (Oct 12), the weekly expiry (Oct 13) and results from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank (Oct 17).
Levels: options traders have built the ceiling at **23,000** and the floor at **22,700** (it moved up from 22,500). A close above 23,000 and the 20-day average (23,147) would start to repair the trend. A fall back below 22,700 and then 22,500 would mean yesterday's new floor failed

sections.title: Bottom line
sections.body: The dashboard is **neutral (+6)** with low confidence. The price trend is clearly down, but options traders and domestic funds are supporting the market, and FIIs are so heavily positioned for a fall that a sharp rebound is possible if they start buying back. Expected swings are moderate: India VIX is about 13.6, at the 64th percentile of the past year. The main risk is today's RBI decision, along with high US bond rates and $100 oil, which keep FIIs selling.
